checks.check: 3d ties 1/2 in the B known score (B_same / B_indep) - STUDY DEFECT
checks.detail: laws.build sets post = m1 / (m1 + m0) from float masses, and b_known ranks that float. Wires whose posteriors are exactly equal (in the float law and in the specification) get posteriors differing in the last bits, so b_known orders pairs that must tie: 18 of 52 views split float-law ties (e.g. REF|0.5|skewed L16: 8 exact levels -> 15 floats). Against the specification, 15 of 32 dA = 0 comparisons give B differences that are not identically 0 (the exact-tie known score gives d = 0 on every sample): IND|0.2|skewed (3), REF|*|skewed (6), RED|*|skewed pair-income (2), COMP occupation-income (all 4 laws). Over the affected comparisons (parts 2 and 3, own samples): at n = 2,000, SD of d up to 0.022, |d| >= 0.020 in up to 37% of samples, R2SE resolved 89/2100 pooled (4.2%; at most 10% per comparison); at n = 20,000, SD up to 0.0093, M20 up to 5%, R2SE 45/780 pooled (5.8%; at most 25% per comparison, R = 20-40). The exact-tie known score gives 0 for all of these. B stays unbiased (mean deviations within about 2 MCSE of 0) and A, C, D are unaffected. Fix suggestion: rank B by the exact tie structure (e.g. group wires by the internal q, which is bitwise tied in REF / RED / IND, or use rationals; COMP needs exactly centred u, v), then recompute B rows; C and D rows need no change.
